challenged_boundary: WP900 sealed successor -> WP206 canonical write/readback -> claimed restart/recovery promotion

source_observation.same_store_fact: persist_sealed_successor_and_readback writes and reloads through the same CanonicalPersistentAgencyStore instance and therefore the same live SQLite connection.
source_observation.same_process_replay_fact: test_replay_is_idempotent_for_exact_same_successor_bytes invokes the adapter twice without closing/reopening the store or terminating the process.
source_observation.credit_fence: The adapter correctly emits target_host_execution=NOT_OBSERVED, runtime_credit=0 and whole_system_acceptance=false.

candidate_falsifier.hypothesis: Repository same-connection write/readback can pass while fresh-process restart/recovery fails due to commit durability, path/fingerprint drift, schema initialization ordering, stale authority metadata, WAL/journal handling, or WP901 ingress differences.
required_discriminator: Process A opens the exact canonical DB through the admitted resolver/fingerprint path, persists a WP900-sealed successor via the existing WP206 adapter, records exact source/tree SHA, canonical path, device/inode, authority receipt hash, checkpoint ids/digests and exits completely.
Do not reuse Process A Python objects, sqlite3 connection, CanonicalPersistentAgencyStore instance, in-memory seal object or fixture state.

Process B starts fresh, resolves/fingerprints the same DB independently, verifies path plus device/inode continuity or explicitly classified replacement semantics, then loads the persisted successor through the accepted WP901/WP206 recovery/readback ingress.
Require exact successor checkpoint id, digest and previous_checkpoint_id to match the Process A sealed subject before granting restart/recovery credit.

Add a crash-window variant where Process A terminates immediately after the canonical write commit and before the integration adapter's same-process readback; Process B must either recover the committed successor exactly or fail closed without inventing a success receipt.
A successful same-process adapter test must never satisfy this discriminator.
falsifying_outcomes: fresh process cannot resolve/load the successor that same-process readback observed
fresh process resolves a different canonical DB authority without an explicit replacement contract
checkpoint bytes/digest/parent lineage differ after reopen
WP901 reports recovery success from metadata/cache without loading the exact persisted row
crash after commit but before same-process readback yields ambiguous or duplicated successor authority

counterhypothesis.statement: If SQLite commit durability, canonical path/fingerprint identity and the WP901/WP206 fresh-open ingress are already equivalent to the same live-store readback, the two-process discriminator will pass without product code changes.
counterhypothesis.value: That result would legitimately advance evidence from repository-component integration toward restart/runtime evidence while preserving one canonical state authority.

duplicate_authority_check: No second store, scheduler, recovery authority or active mutation claim introduced; review only.
single_most_important_correction: Before any WP900/WP206/WP901 runtime promotion, require an exact-source two-process persist -> terminate/crash -> fresh-open WP901/WP206 readback test that cannot reuse the original SQLite connection or in-memory objects.
